# Repertoire overlap {#sec-overlap-sharing}

Clonotypes seen in more than one sample. Within a patient this reflects genuine clonal
persistence across timepoints or tissues; across patients it usually reflects public
clonotypes with high generation probability rather than a shared response.

## Sample overlap

```{python}
#| output: asis
#| echo: false

_ol = rb_read('repertoire', 'overlap_samples.tsv')
if _ol is None or not {'sample_a', 'sample_b', 'jaccard'} <= set(_ol.columns):
    rb_note("No sample overlap table available (produced by REPERTOIRE_METRICS).")
else:
    m = _ol.pivot_table(index='sample_a', columns='sample_b', values='jaccard', aggfunc='first')
    m.index = rb_label(m.index)
    m.columns = rb_label(m.columns)
    fig = go.Figure(go.Heatmap(z=m.values, x=list(m.columns), y=list(m.index),
                               colorscale=[[0, 'white'], [0.5, '#fee391'], [1, '#cb181d']],
                               hovertemplate='%{y} vs %{x}<br>Jaccard: %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>'))
    _rb_layout(fig, "Sample repertoire overlap (Jaccard)", 560, xaxis=dict(title='', tickangle=-45),
               yaxis=dict(title=''))
```

**Figure `{python} fig_no()`. Sample overlap.** Jaccard index between every pair of samples
(labelled by alias): the share of unique clonotypes found in both (0 = none, 1 = identical); hover
a tile for the exact value. Expect a visible block within each patient
(clones persisting across timepoints or tissues) and near-zero values between patients; a bright
cell between two patients suggests contamination or a sample swap.

## Most shared clonotypes

```{python}
#| output: asis
#| echo: false

_cs = rb_read('repertoire', 'clone_sharing.tsv')
if _cs is None:
    rb_note("No top shared clones table available.")
else:
    rb_text(f"The 50 clonotypes found in the most samples ({len(_cs):,} shared clonotypes in total).")
    rb_table(_cs.head(50))
```

**Table `{python} tab_no()`. Most shared clonotypes**, ordered by the number of samples they occur in. Clonotypes
shared between patients are usually public sequences with a high generation probability (see
the convergent-selection plot above); those shared only within one patient are persistent clones.
